data.narrative:
Slate Auto is a Series C transportation company founded by Miles Arnone, Will Barker, and Jeff Wilke (former CEO Worldwide Consumer, Amazon). The company has raised $1.4B to date. The transportation sector peer set includes 8 private companies—notably Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, ZeroAvia, and Harbinger—with no public comparables identified.

Valuation analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, as peer-median triangulation was not applicable. The transportation sector yielded only 3 same-sector peers, none of which met sufficient overlap criteria across stage, timing, and valuation tier to support robust median benchmarking. The stage-progression method applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier from the $1.4B total raised proxy, reflecting typical Series C-to-later-stage progression. This yields an implied valuation of $2.4B.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $2.0B to $2.7B, centered on $2.4B. Key uncertainties stem from the method count of one: reliance on a single triangulation approach limits cross-validation. The lack of near-peer valuation data in a nascent, capital-intensive sector compounds uncertainty around stage-progression assumptions. Validation would benefit from operational metrics (unit economics, production roadmap, customer concentration) and refined comparability within frontier transportation sub-verticals. The $1.4B raised proxy itself merits scrutiny as a valuation anchor in a rapidly evolving space.
